note: Real bank downloads, anonymised with `npm run anonymize` (see docs/import-export-design.md, Phase A). Every value is synthetic or a generic banking word; dates are shifted by whole weeks; balances are recomputed. These are checked on every test run and are never regenerated by the seed.

statements.source: Bank 1, chequing: a plain OFX 1.0.2 download under Microsoft Money's old .aso extension; CRLF; an empty <ACCTTYPE>; a <USERKEY> credential and <MESSAGE> lines the policy drops; FITIDs that are long digit runs
Bank 1, chequing: the same statement as Quicken Web Connect, with <INTU.BID>
Bank 1, chequing: the same statement as QuickBooks Web Connect (byte-identical to the QFX)

Bank 2, chequing: OFX 1.x with LF line endings, a blank line after every <MEMO>, a DTSTART later than DTEND, mixed-case payees with trailing store and reference numbers, FITIDs mixing letters and digits
Bank 2, chequing: the same statement as QuickBooks Web Connect (byte-identical to the QFX)
Bank 1, chequing: no header row, every cell quoted, LF endings, ISO dates, separate debit and credit columns written as magnitudes, a running balance

Bank 2, chequing: a UTF-8 BOM, CRLF, a 7-column header whose first column is a filter description filled only on the first row, a type column (Debit/Credit), one signed amount column and a running balance

Microsoft Money, chequing, the 'loose' export: a single !Type:Bank block with no !Account, ISO dates (a Canadian locale), amounts grouped with commas, EFT/DEP-style number codes beside cheque numbers, transfers as [Account], 16 split records (S/E/$), cleared marks * and X; payees, memos and category segments at full length

Microsoft Money, the same statement as the 'strict' export: category segments capped at fifteen characters while payees and memos keep their full length — so dialect has to be judged per field, not per file
